Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כל היכא דתני הכל, כולהו מייתי להו בשמעתא קמייתא דערכין, ומפרש הכל לאתויי מאי. והכל שוחטין דמתניתין, פליגי בה אמוראי בגמרא, למר לאתויי טמא בחולין, ולמר לאתויי כותי או מומר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: All may slaughter - Wherever [the Mishnah] teaches 'all,' they [the Gemara] cite all of these instances in the first sugya of Arachin, and explain what 'all' comes to include. And [as for] 'All may slaughter' of our Mishnah, the Amoraim disagree about it in the Gemara: according to one, it comes to include a tamei person [slaughtering] non-sacred animals; and according to the other, it comes to include a Samaritan (Kuthite) or an apostate.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: And all of them - The Gemara explains what [is meant by] "and all of them."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.hebrew: ושחיטתן כשרה דיעבד - בתמיה. וקשה, רישא דמשמע דההוא דאתרבי מהכל לכתחלה אתרבי, ואילו סיפא משמע דכי מרבינן מהכל דיעבד מרבינן לה, אבל לכתחלה לא אתרבי. והא ליכא למימר כולה מתניתין לכתחלה וחדא קתני, דכיון דתנא הכל שוחטין פשיטא דכשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.english: And their slaughtering is valid after the fact - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question. And it is difficult: the first clause implies that whoever is included by "all" is included [to slaughter] ab initio, whereas the latter clause implies that when we include [someone] from "all," we include him only after the fact, but he is not included ab initio. And you cannot say that the entire Mishnah speaks of ab initio [permission] and is teaching a single point, for since it already taught "all may slaughter," it is obvious that the slaughtering is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.hebrew: וכל הכל לכתחלה הוא - דתקשה לך ולא תוכל לומר כולה דיעבד, וה"ק: הכל תורת שחיטה נוהגת בהן, שאם שחטו אותן הפסולין דמתרבי תהא שחיטתן כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.english: And [is] every [instance of] 'all' [indicative of it being permitted] ab initio - For it would [otherwise] be difficult for you, and you could not say that the whole [teaching] is [meant only] after the fact either. Rather, this is what he [Rav Acha] is saying: [By] 'all,' the law of slaughter fully applies to them [i.e., to those basically fit to perform it], such that if those disqualified people who are included [under the extension of 'all'] performed the slaughter, their slaughter would [nonetheless] be valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.hebrew: אלא הכל ממירים - מי מצית למימר לכתחלה יביא בהמת חולין אצל בהמת קדשים ויאמר זו תמורת זו? הכל דתמורה מפרש התם לאתויי יורש, שממיר בקרבן אביו לאחר מיתת אביו, דהתם תנן: אין ממירין בשל אחרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.english: Rather, all may effect temurah - Can you possibly say that, from the outset, one may bring a non-sacred animal alongside a consecrated animal and say, "This one is a substitute for that one"? [Rather,] the word "all" regarding temurah is expounded there [in tractate Temurah] to include an heir who effects temurah with his father's offering after his father's death, for there we learned: one may not effect temurah with another's [animal].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:4.english: Bad - [i.e., an animal] possessing a blemish.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - דעקר להכל דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא. אבל הכל שוחטין בדוכתיה קאי, דכל כמה דלא עקר ליה, ותנא לא שיהו הפסולים רשאים לשחוט כדעקר התם, משמע דלכתחלה רבינהו, והדר תני ושחיטתן כשרה, דמשמע דיעבד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, as it taught the reason - [this] negates [the implication of] "everyone" in the opening clause, so that you should not say it means [that it is permitted] ab initio. But [in our mishnah], "all may slaughter" retains its [plain] sense - for as long as [the mishnah] does not negate it, and the tanna did not teach [something like] "this does not mean the disqualified are permitted to slaughter," the way it negated [the implication] there, it implies that ab initio it includes them. And then it teaches "and their slaughtering is valid," which implies after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: לא שהאדם רשאי - דכתיב לא יחליפנו, ורישא הכי קאמר: הכל דין תמורה נוהגת בהם. והא דתנא ברישא הכל ממירין, ואיצטריך ליה תו לפרושי לא שהאדם רשאי כו', ולא נקט ברישא לשון קצרה הכל שהמירו תמורתם תמורה - לשון התנאים הוא זה, כמו הכל שוחטין הכל סומכין הכל חייבין, הלכך הכא אע"ג דהוצרך להאריך, לא שינה התנא את לשונו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: Not that a person is permitted - For it is written, "he shall not exchange it" (Leviticus 27:10). And the opening statement means to say as follows: the law of substitution applies to all of them. And as for the fact that the Tanna taught at the outset, "all may substitute," and it was necessary for him to further explain, "not that a person is permitted," etc. - [that is because] he did not use at the outset the concise wording, "whoever substituted, their substitute is a valid substitute"; rather, this [wording, 'all may substitute'] is the style of the Tannaim, like "all may slaughter," "all may perform semichah," "all are obligated." Therefore here, even though he needed to elaborate, the Tanna did not change his style.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:3.english: Is substituted [מומר] - The second animal becomes consecrated, and both [animals] are holy.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:4.english: And he receives the forty [lashes] - because of the prohibition "he shall not exchange it" (Vayikra 27:10).

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.hebrew: הכל מעריכין - התם מפרש לאתויי מופלא סמוך לאיש, קטן היודע להפלות לשם מי מקדישין. ואם סמוך לפרקו הוא, כגון בן י"ב שנה ויום אחד, דבריו קיימין, אע"פ שעדיין קטן הוא עד י"ג שנה ויום אחד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.english: All may make valuations - There [in Arachin] it is explained that ["all"] comes to include a mufla samukh le-ish [a minor approaching adulthood] - a minor who knows how to distinguish for whose sake he is consecrating. And if he is close to his [physical] maturity, such as one who is twelve years and one day old, his words stand, even though he is still legally a minor until thirteen years and one day old.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.hebrew: מעריכין - תורת מעריכין עליהם, שאם אמר ערכי עלי או ערך פלוני עלי נדרו קיים, ואע"ג דקטן הוא זה הנודר, חייב ליתן כפי שנים של נערך, והדמים קצובין בפרשה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.english: May be valuated - The law of valuations applies to them, that if one said, 'my valuation is upon me,' or 'so-and-so's valuation is upon me,' his vow stands; and even though this vower is a minor, he is obligated to pay according to the years of the one being appraised, and the amounts are fixed in the passage.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.hebrew: הכל נערכין - יש להם ערך, ואפילו מוכה שחין שאינו שוה כלום לימכר בשוק, יש לו ערך הכתוב בפרשה. ואם אמר על עצמו ערכי עלי, או אמר על אחר ערך מוכה שחין זה עלי, לא אמרינן הואיל ודמים אין לו ערך נמי אין לו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.english: All are subject to valuation - they have a [fixed, Scripturally-set] value; and even one afflicted with boils, who is worth nothing to be sold in the market, has the value written in the passage [i.e., the Torah's fixed valuation applies to him]. And if he said of himself, "my valuation is upon me," or said of another, "the valuation of this person afflicted with boils is upon me," we do not say that since he has no [market] worth, he also has no [fixed] valuation.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.hebrew: הכל נודרים - דמי עלי או דמי פלוני עלי. והתם מפרש דאיידי דבעי למיתני הכל נידרין, תנא נמי הכל נודרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.english: All vow - [i.e., one who says] "my [market] value is incumbent upon me [to donate]" or "so-and-so's value is incumbent upon me." And there [in tractate Arachin] it explains that since it needed to teach "all may be vowed [i.e., made the object of such a vow]," it also taught "all vow."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.hebrew: הכל נידרים - כל אדם השוה כלום יש לו דמים, ואם אמר דמי עלי, או אמר על אחר דמי פלוני עלי, נותן לפי מה שהוא נמכר בשוק. ואפילו היה הנידר זה פחות מבן חדש, ואמר דמי תינוק זה עלי, יתן דמיו, ואע"פ שאין פחות מבן חדש נערך. ואם אמר ערכו עלי, פטור מכלום, שלא נתנה בו תורה ערך, דכתיב (ויקרא כז) ואם מבן חדש ועד בן חמש שנים, דמים מיהא יש לו לפי שויו, ואם אמר בתורת דמים נותן דמיו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.english: All can be vowed [about] - Any person who is worth anything has a "damim" (monetary worth) value. And if he said, "My worth is upon me [as a vow]," or said of another, "So-and-so's worth is upon me," he pays according to what that person would sell for in the market. And even if the one being vowed about is less than a month old, and he said, "This infant's worth is upon me," he must pay his worth, even though [an infant] less than a month old is not subject to a fixed Torah valuation (erech). But if he said, "His erech is upon me," he is exempt from paying anything, because the Torah did not assign an erech to him, as it is written (Vayikra 27), "And if from a month old to five years old..." [implying that a fixed valuation applies only from one month of age]. He does, however, have a "damim" worth, according to his value, and if he vowed in terms of "damim," he pays his worth.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:6.english: There will be no sin in you - [This implies:] but if you do vow, there will be sin in you.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.hebrew: טוב אשר לא תדור - לעיל מיניה כתיב "את אשר תדור שלם", ואפילו הכי, "טוב אשר לא תדור", שמא תדור ולא תשלם. הכי מפרש ליה רבי מאיר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: Better that you not vow - Just before this it is written, "That which you vow, fulfill" (Ecclesiastes 5:3), and even so, [it says] "Better that you not vow" - lest you vow and not pay. This is how Rabbi Meir explains it [i.e., reconciles the two adjacent verses].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה - מנודר ומשלם, ומנודר ואינו משלם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than this and than that - ["This"] is one bound by a vow who pays, and ["that"] is one bound by a vow who does not pay.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:3.english: He does not vow at all - For one who is accustomed to making vows will eventually come to [violate the prohibition of] "he shall not profane his word" (Numbers 30:3).

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר טוב מזה ומזה נודר ומשלם - דהכי משמע, טוב אשר לא תדור משתדור ולא תשלם, אבל משתדור ותשלם לא, שהוא טוב מכולם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Better than both this and that is one who vows and pays - For this is what [the verse] implies: '[It is] better that you not vow' than [that] you vow and not pay; but it does not say this compared to [one who] vows and pays - i.e., [the verse does] not [mean] that [not vowing] is better than all of them [including vowing and paying].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:5.hebrew: ואפילו ר' יהודה לא קאמר אלא דאמר הרי זו - דאם מתה או נגנבה, אינו חייב באחריותה. אי נמי, כיון דאפרשה, תו לא הדר ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:5.english: And even R' Yehuda said this only where he said, 'This is it' - for if it died or was stolen, he is not liable to replace it. Alternatively, since he has [already] set it aside, he can no longer retract from it.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כתוב בהלכות ארץ ישראל דנשים לא ישחטו מפני שדעתן קלות, ואין נראה, דאפילו במוקדשין שוחטות לכתחלה, כדאמרינן פרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:) כל הפסולים ששחטו דיעבד אין לכתחלה לא, ורמינהי: ושחט - מלמד שהשחיטה כשרה כו', ומשני: הוא הדין דאפילו לכתחלה, אלא משום דבעי למיתני טמא במוקדשים דלכתחלה לא, תנא נמי ששחטו, ולא קאמר משום דבעי למיתני נשים דתנא להו ברישא, אלא ודאי משום דנשים שוחטות לכתחלה אפילו במוקדשין. והא דלא קתני "הכל שוחטין אחד אנשים ואחד נשים" כדקתני בתמורה (דף ב.), התם אצטריך למיתנייה כדפירש בריש תמורה משום דכל הפרשה כולה נאמרה בלשון זכר, אבל הכא אין חידוש באשה יותר מבאיש. ובפרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:) גבי קדשים איצטריך למיתני נשים, משום דבשאר עבודות נשים פסולות אפילו כהנות:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: All may slaughter - It is written in Halachot Eretz Yisrael that women should not slaughter, because their minds are flighty. But this does not seem right, for even with consecrated animals they may slaughter ab initio, as we say in the chapter "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 31b): all those disqualified [from the other sacrificial services] who slaughtered - after the fact, yes; ab initio, no. And they raise a contradiction: "and he shall slaughter" - this teaches that the slaughtering is valid, etc. And they answer: the same applies even ab initio; rather, because [the mishnah there] wanted to teach [the law of] a tamei person with consecrated animals, that ab initio it is not [permitted], it therefore also phrased [the law regarding other disqualified people] in terms of "who slaughtered" [i.e., after the fact]. And it did not say that [the reason for that phrasing] is because it wanted to teach about women - whom it had [already] taught at the beginning [of that mishnah] - rather, it must be because women may slaughter ab initio, even with consecrated animals. And as for why [our mishnah] does not state "All may slaughter, both men and women," as is stated in Temurah (2a) - there it was necessary to state it, as is explained at the beginning of Temurah, because that entire passage [of the Torah] is stated in the masculine. But here there is no novelty in [including] a woman beyond [what applies to] a man. And in the chapter "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 31b), regarding consecrated animals, it was necessary to state [explicitly] "women," because with regard to the other sacrificial services, women are disqualified - even the daughters of priests.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.hebrew: שמא יקלקלו כו' - בגמרא (לקמן חולין יב:) דייק מדקתני "שמא יקלקלו" ולא קתני "שמא קלקלו", ש"מ אין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה. ופ"ה אפילו אחרים רואין אותן. וק' לפירושו, דהא מסיפא שמעינן לה: וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן כו', דמשמע דיעבד דוקא. וליכא למימר דדיעבד נקט משום טמא במוקדשין או אין מומחין, אבל חש"ו אפילו לכתחלה שוחטין באחרים רואין אותן, דהא רבא הוא דדייק שמא קלקלו לא קתני, ולרבא לא קאי וכולן ששחטו אלא אחש"ו, כדאמרינן בגמרא. וי"מ דגרס לקמן "רבה", אבל רבא לא דייק בין יקלקלו לקלקלו, כי היכי דלא חייש בהא דלא קתני "ואם שחטו". ור"ת מפרש דאין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה לשחוט אפילו כדי להשליך לכלבים, דלמא אתי למיכל, שיטעו להכשיר שחיטתן מתוך שיראו שמוסרים להן, כדפטר לקמן שחיטתן מכסוי, דלמא אתי למימר שחיטה מעלייתא היא. וניחא השתא, דבאין אחרים רואין אותן עסקינן ברישא:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: Lest they spoil, etc. - In the Gemara (below, Chullin 12b), it is inferred from the fact that it teaches "lest they will spoil" and does not teach "lest they had spoiled," that this tells us: non-sacred animals are not handed over to them [a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor] to slaughter ab initio. And Rashi explains that this holds even when others are watching them. And this is difficult according to his explanation, for we already learn this from the latter clause [of the mishnah]: "and all of them, if they slaughtered while others were watching them...," etc., which implies specifically after the fact [but not ab initio]. And one cannot say that it phrases this in terms of "after the fact" [only] on account of [the cases of] a tamei person [slaughtering] consecrated animals, or one who is not an expert - while a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor may actually slaughter even ab initio when others are watching them - for it is Rava himself who infers that it does not teach "lest they had spoiled," and according to Rava, [the clause] "and all of them who slaughtered" refers only to a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, as we say in the Gemara. And some explain that the text further on reads "Rabbah" [rather than "Rava"], and that Rava does not make any inference between "they will spoil" and "they had spoiled," just as he is not troubled here by the fact that it does not teach "and if they slaughtered." And Rabbeinu Tam explains that non-sacred animals are not handed over to them to slaughter ab initio even in order to throw [the meat] to the dogs, lest people come to eat from it - that is, they might mistakenly validate their slaughter upon seeing that [non-sacred animals] are handed over to them, just as [the Gemara] later exempts their slaughter from the requirement of covering the blood, lest one come to say that it is a proper act of slaughter. And it now fits well that the first clause [of the mishnah] deals with a case where others are not watching them.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - פירש בקונטרס דעקר ליה להכל דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא. ולשון "כדקתני טעמא" לא משמע כפירושו. ומה שפירש נמי במסקנא גבי "דאי דיעבד, תרתי דיעבד למה לי", ואע"ג דבתמורה נמי תני והדר מפרש, התם לא תנא כי האי גוונא "הכל ממירין" ו"תמורתן תמורה" גבי הדדי. ואי משום "לא שהאדם רשאי להמיר" משום דבעי לאסוקי "וסופג את הארבעים" לאשמועינן דלוקין על לאו שאין בו מעשה, אין נראה, דמשום "וסופג את הארבעים" לחודיה לא הוה ליה למיתני תרתי דיעבד, דהוה מצי למיתני "הכל ממירים והממיר סופג את הארבעים". ועוד, דבריש תמורה (דף ב.) פריך: הכל ממירים לכתחלה, ולא שהאדם רשאי להמיר דיעבד? ומשני התם: רב יהודה הכי קתני, "הכל מתפיסים בתמורה, אחד שוגג ואחד מזיד". והוה ליה לשנויי דתנא ליה משום "וסופג את הארבעים", כדפירש בקונטרס כאן. ונראה לרבינו תם דשינויא דהכא הוי כההיא דתמורה, והכי קאמר: התם כדקתני טעמא, דלהכי תנא "הכל ממירים" דמשמע לכתחלה, לאשמעינן שאפילו המיר במזיד, דהיינו לכתחלה, מומר, דלא תימא ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר, כדאמרן בהתודה (מנחות פא.). וקשה לפירושו, דבסוף פרק קמא דתמורה (דף יג.) משמע דמן הדין ראוי להיות תמורה במזיד יותר מבשוגג, דקאמר "יהיה" לרבות שוגג כמזיד. ויש לומר דלענין בהמה שתהא כשרה למזבח פשוט לן שוגג יותר ממזיד, אי נמי התם איירי במזיד ולא אתרו ביה דלא הוו ארבעים בכתפיה, וההוא מזיד פשוט לן יותר משוגג:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, as it explicitly teaches the reason - Rashi explains that this negates the "all" of the first clause [of the Temurah mishnah], so that you should not say it means ab initio. But the wording "as it explicitly teaches the reason" does not imply his interpretation. Nor does what he also explains at the conclusion, regarding [the question] "if it means only after the fact, why does it need two statements of 'after the fact'?" And even though tractate Temurah itself likewise teaches [the mishnah] and then explains it, there it does not teach in this manner - "all may make a temurah exchange" and "their exchange is a valid exchange" - juxtaposed with each other. And if [the reason for saying] "not that a person is permitted to make an exchange" is that it wants to lead into "and he receives forty lashes," to teach us that one is lashed for a prohibition that involves no action, this does not seem right: on account of "and he receives forty lashes" alone, it would not have needed to teach two statements of "after the fact," since it could simply have taught "all may make a temurah exchange, and one who makes the exchange receives forty lashes." Furthermore, at the beginning of tractate Temurah (2a), it asks whether "all may make a temurah exchange" [means] ab initio, and whether "not that a person is permitted to make an exchange" [means] after the fact - and it answers there that Rav Yehuda meant to teach: "all may consecrate through a temurah exchange, whether unwittingly or intentionally." It ought instead to have answered that [the mishnah] phrased it that way for the sake of [concluding with] "and he receives forty lashes," as Rashi explained here. Rabbeinu Tam holds that the resolution here is like that one in Temurah, and that this is the meaning: "there, as it explicitly teaches the reason" - that is why it taught "all may make a temurah exchange," which implies ab initio, so as to teach that even one who made the exchange intentionally - that is, ab initio - has effected a valid exchange; lest you think that he merely receives forty lashes on his back while [the original animal] remains as it was, as we said in [the chapter] "HaTodah" (Menachot 81a). This explanation is difficult, though, for at the end of the first chapter of Temurah (13a) it implies that, strictly speaking, a temurah is more fittingly effected when done intentionally than unwittingly, since it says that [the word] "it shall be" comes to include the unwitting case like the intentional one. One may answer that with regard to the animal's fitness for the altar, it is obvious to us that an unwitting exchange [is more valid] than an intentional one; or else, that passage deals with an intentional act for which the person was not forewarned - so that there would be no forty lashes on his back - and that sort of intentional act is obviously [more valid] to us than an unwitting one.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: וסופג את הארבעים - וא"ת הוה ליה למימר "וסופג שמונים", דהא תרי לאוי כתיב: "לא יחליפנו" ו"לא ימיר". ויש לומר דחד בשלו וחד בשל חברו, כדאמר בתמורה (דף ט.), וכגון דאמר חברו: "כל הרוצה להמיר בבהמתו ימיר", דבענין אחר אין ממירין בשל אחרים, והכי איתא בהדיא בתמורה פ"ק:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: And he receives forty lashes - One might ask: it should have said "and he receives eighty lashes," for behold, two prohibitions are written: "he shall not exchange it" and "he shall not substitute it" [Leviticus 27:10]. And one can answer that one [prohibition] applies to [substituting] with his own [animal], and one applies to [substituting] with his fellow's [animal], as is stated in Temurah (9a) - namely, a case where the fellow said, "Whoever wishes may effect a substitution with his [i.e., my] animal." For otherwise, one cannot effect a temurah with another's animal [and incur lashes for it]. And this is stated explicitly in Temurah, first chapter.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:1.hebrew: וכתיב טוב אשר לא תדור - מעיקרא מייתי מדברי תורה, והדר מייתי מדברי קבלה:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: And it is written, "It is better that you not vow" - At first [the Gemara] cites [a proof] from the words of the Torah, and afterward it cites [a proof] from the words of tradition (i.e., the Prophets and Writings).

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה שאינו נודר כל עיקר - פ"ה דלעיל מיניה כתיב "את אשר תדור שלם", ואפילו הכי "טוב אשר לא תדור", שמא תדור ולא תשלם. וקשה לר"ת, דלא מייתי בגמרא ההוא קרא כלל. ונראה לר"ת דכולי מלתא דריש מהאי קרא, דהוה ליה למיכתב "טוב אשר לא תדור" משתדור, ואנא ידענא דמשתדור ולא תשלם קאמר, אלא להכי קאמר "ולא תשלם" לגלויי על משתדור, דמשתדור כדרך הנודרין קאמר שנודרין ומשלמין, כדאמר גבי שכיר ותושב: בא זה ולימד על זה (קדושין דף ד.):
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than both this and that is one who does not vow at all - Rashi explains: in the verse before it, it is written, "That which you vow, fulfill" (Ecclesiastes 5:3), and nevertheless, "Better that you not vow" (Ecclesiastes 5:4) - lest you vow and not pay. And this is difficult according to Rabbeinu Tam, for the Gemara does not cite that [earlier] verse at all. And it seems to Rabbeinu Tam that the entire matter is derived from this verse alone. For it should have written [simply], "Better that you not vow" than "vow" - and I would [already] know that it means than vowing and not paying [since that is the concern at hand]. Rather, [Scripture] therefore says "and not pay" in order to reveal [the meaning of] "than vowing" - that "than vowing" is stated in the ordinary manner of vowers, namely, that they vow and [normally] pay - just as is said regarding a hired worker and a resident alien: "this one comes and teaches about that one" (Kiddushin 4a).
